units.text: We'll compare an answer grounded in an internal policy with a model trained for a different task. In the grounded-answer case, begin with the approved policy document, sync it, and verify the current version can be found before trusting an answer.

The application checks the caller and filters retrieval to permitted sources. Use the relevant passage to ground the answer and include the source where supported. If the current approved passage is missing or conflicting, return a safe no-answer instead of guessing.

For a custom model, split the labeled examples so the evaluation can test more than memorization. Train and tune on the appropriate split, then compare the validation result with the agreed release criteria. If it misses, improve and evaluate again.

Only after the model passes do you deploy. Choose a real-time endpoint for interactive predictions or batch inference for a collection of records. Test the deployed result rather than inferring production quality from a training run.

Monitor model quality and data drift after deployment. SageMaker Model Monitor is only available to existing customers; choose an available monitoring setup for new designs. Use the collected evidence and an approved review before deciding to retrain.
